choices: An object the JVM created for the loaded class — the same object `getClass()` returns on any instance.
A compile-time literal that the compiler replaces with the class's fully qualified name.
A new object created each time the expression is evaluated, describing the class's shape.
A reference to the class file on disk, opened lazily when a member is requested.
explanation: The JVM creates exactly one `Class` per loaded class, which is why `a.getClass() == Account.class` is true. It can be stored, compared, passed to a method, and asked for its name, superclass, fields, methods, modifiers and annotations. Everything `javac` knew is still there, with one large exception — the type arguments that Section 27.2.1 shows were erased.
